title: postfix ! before a member CALL compiles and runs: the allowance never ended at the call
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md row that cites it (§4.13) keeps resolving; the name records what this program used to be, not what it is. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the five-condition placement walk this case certified, and DECISIONS.md §Typed failures records the withdrawal as the point of no return: `!` is accepted in any expression position, and three conditions refuse it — no enclosing Result channel, non-Result operand provenance, and an enclosing `catch`. WHY IT NOW PASSES, stated as a fact about the lowering rather than as a quotation: `lookup("ada")!` is evaluated unconditionally, exactly once, and with nothing effectful to its left in the statement, so the shipped early-return lowering hoists its guard to the front of the `const` and the emitted program calls `lookup`, checks, and then calls `.trim()` — the authored order, unchanged. The member CALL was never the thing that made this unsound; the old rule refused it because its walk stopped at the nearest statement through an allow-list of seven node kinds, and a call was not on the list. Its accepted twin postfix-bang-as-a-property-access-object-is-accepted is the identical program with `.length`, and the pair no longer records a distinction — both compile, and keeping both is what shows that. MARKER RETIRED 2026-08-30, and the fork's half of the withdrawal is what retired it. `safeUnwrapPlacement` and `isInRepeatedLoopHeader` are deleted from `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` and replaced by the SAME three predicates the reference applies — `conditionallyEvaluatedPosition`, `repeatedlyEvaluatedPosition` and `precededByUnhoistedEffect` — so both backends now accept this program for the same stated reason. Re-derived by RUNNING both backends over this case, not by reading either one's source: the fork's predicates were written against measured behaviour and checked against the reference on the three programs that keep the residue alive (`while (next()!) {}`, `maybe ?? r!`, `g() + r!`), each of which both backends still refuse with the same code at the same position.
